title: Custom React.memo Simulator
problemStatement: Implement `memoComponent(Component, arePropsEqual = shallowEqual)` that returns a wrapper function tracking the last rendered props and result. If incoming props are equal to previous props, return the cached result without executing `Component`.
interviewTrap: Not allowing a custom `arePropsEqual` comparator. React allows developers to provide custom comparison functions for complex objects.

testCases.name: Re-uses cached render when props are unchanged
testCases.input: render twice with identical props runs component once
testCases.testFn: let renders = 0; const Comp = (props) => { renders++; return props.name; }; const Memo = memoComponent(Comp, shallowEqual); Memo({ name: 'Alpha' }); Memo({ name: 'Alpha' }); return renders;

testCases.name: Re-renders when props change
testCases.testFn: let renders = 0; const Comp = (props) => { renders++; return props.name; }; const Memo = memoComponent(Comp, shallowEqual); Memo({ name: 'Alpha' }); Memo({ name: 'Beta' }); return renders;

testCases.name: Respects custom comparison function
testCases.testFn: let renders = 0; const Comp = (p) => { renders++; return p.id; }; const Memo = memoComponent(Comp, (a, b) => a.id === b.id); Memo({ id: 1, title: 'Old' }); Memo({ id: 1, title: 'New' }); return renders;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: By default, when a parent component renders, all its child components re-render recursively regardless of whether their props changed. `React.memo` bails out only if all props are shallowly equal.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Component Memoization & Skip Render Decision.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
